Lydia / Rahul —

Thanks for the kickoff call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the explicit throughput/latency scenarios we should size for on your private deployment and call out networking/failover constraints up-front so we can produce a single recommended cluster topology and an ops playbook.

Quick asks from us to firm up estimates:
- Target steady-state QPS and peak burst QPS (requests/sec) and the typical token length per request (mean / p95).
- Required latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for inference responses.
- Desired availability during regional failover (RPO/RTO expectations) and whether cross-datacenter failover is allowed.
- Any regulatory constraints (log retention, no-egress) that would block cross-region autoscaling.

Initial notes from Redwood:
- We'll size per "performance envelope" rather than per-model where possible (e.g., conversational 128-token average vs. long-form 1k-token).
- Networking: we recommend 25Gbps+ NICs per GPU host, RDMA when low inter-node latency is required for KV cache sharing, and ToR switch fabric with <1ms east-west latency for predictable batching.
- Scaling policy: we typically target sustained GPU util 70-80% and queue depth triggers for burst scale-ups; fallback model variants should be included (smaller quantized model) to preserve latency SLOs when capacity is constrained.

Can you send the numbers above by EOD? We'll draft two scenarios (conservative and aggressive) and a failover plan for cross-rack or cross-DC events.

Thanks,

Thanks Soojin —

Numbers from our side (production baseline plus expected ramp):
- Typical request profile: 70% short chat (mean ~120 tokens), 25% medium (mean ~512 tokens), 5% long-form (mean ~2,048 tokens).
- Steady-state QPS: 180 requests/sec (global for our cluster during business hours). Peak burst (marketing/promo): up to 480 requests/sec sustained for ~3–6 minutes; spike bursts up to 900 r/s for <1 minute.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 350ms for chat flows (128 tokens); long-form can be relaxed to p95 < 2s.
- Availability: goal is 99.95% for the private cluster; we want cross-DC failover within 10 minutes if primary DC loses service. No cross-border failover (data must stay within US).
- Constraints: we have a colo provider (EdgeHost) that supports 100Gbps uplinks but limited RDMA/VPC direct connectivity; we'll loop in DC ops for topology details.

We'll also share a short MLP trace from last 30 days (attached separately) for tail-traffic analysis.

Folks —

I've sketched three capacity scenarios based on Acme's profile. See attached spreadsheet (20260302-capacity-scenarios.xlsx). High-level assumptions and quick numbers:

Assumptions:
- Reference model: 70B-class decoder (quantized int8) with optimized kernels; batch-friendly runtime.
- Reference HW: A100-80GB or equivalent Ampere instance with 40–48 GB usable for model shards after NVLink overhead.
- Typical request sizes weighted by Lydia's distribution above.

Scenarios (rounded):
1) Conservative (latency-first): target p95 150ms for chat — estimated 24 GPU hosts (A100) to cover steady 180 r/s with headroom for short 3–6 min bursts. Cross-rack redundancy: 3 racks of 8 GPUs each.
2) Balanced (cost/perf): target p95 200ms — ~16 GPU hosts; autoscaling + burst pool reduces committed nodes to 12 with 4 on-demand burst nodes.
3) Aggressive (throughput-first): target p95 250ms — ~10 GPU hosts using larger batching and relaxed p95; depends on RDMA and networking to keep batch latency predictable.

Networking notes:
- To meet short p95 targets we recommend 25–100Gbps NICs on each host, with ToR switches supporting ECMP and low microburst behavior.
- If you need KV cache sharing across nodes for long conversations, RDMA will reduce cross-node transfer latencies and improve effective throughput. Without RDMA, we recommend model placement per-rack to avoid cross-rack KV traffic.

Autoscaling & failover:
- Scale-up triggers: sustained GPU util > 75% for 90s OR request queue depth > 60 for 120s.
- Scale-down: util < 40% for 5m with cool-down to avoid thrash.
- Cross-DC failover: warm standby cluster in secondary DC limited to critical routes (graceful degrade to smaller model variants prioritized by route).

Open questions for DC ops:
- NICs available per host (25/50/100Gbps), ToR buffering behavior, LACP/ECMP config.
- If NVLink/NVSwitch is available at rack-level for multi-GPU aggregation.

I'll update the spreadsheet with per-GPU QPS estimates and a simple TCO model after we confirm NICs and rack density.

-marcus
